main_body: Wooden gong frame: two posts with a top crossbeam and small foot blocks, holding a large round gold gong seen face-on
top_band: Top beam: light red-brown rows 1-2 only, then a mid-brown front face rows 3-4 and a dark shadow row 5. No real top surface on the beam or the feet.
evidence: In the column through the beam, the lighter top is only about 2 rows. That reads as a cap line, not a surface, and is too thin for a frame whose beams must show top faces. The posts are flat vertical strips with no visible top. The feet blocks have only a 1-2 row light edge. The gong is a flat disc drawn face-on. The whole piece reads as an architectural front elevation, not a 3/4 view.

style.evidence: The gong has a good 5-6 step yellow ramp with a highlight and a rim. The wooden frame is much shallower, with about 3 tones. The posts are long flat strips of one colour, 3-4 px wide and more than 20 rows tall, with no grain or knots. Outlines are dark brown, which is acceptable. Tile density is lower than the reference stall and well, which carry grain, tile texture and stone shading across the whole piece.
